meta.title: HAZOP and LOPA of the SEP-V101 unit
meta.scope: From the production manifold (well stream battery limit) through SDV-101, choke HV-100, the demulsifier injection (T-105, P-105) and the inlet heater E-101 to the three-phase separator V-101 and its gas (PV-110 to V-201 / K-201), flare (PV-111, PSV-119, BDV-118), oil (SDV-134, LV-130 to the LP separator) and water (SDV-124, LV-120 to the hydrocyclones) outlets, including utilities (LP steam, instrument air, electrical power).
meta.objective: Identify the hazards and operability problems of the unit, judge their risk, and decide what must be added or changed. For the scenarios that need more than the existing safeguards, check the risk reduction by LOPA.
meta.assump: The unit is operated by trained staff at the design conditions (V-101 at 10.0 bar g, 50 °C). LP steam, instrument air and power are available at start-up. The well stream carries no H2S (assumed). Instruments, trips and PSV-119 are tested on the plan in the maintenance procedure.
meta.protocol: Method: HAZOP to IEC 61882 with full recording. The team takes one node at a time, states its design intent, and applies the guide words to each parameter to find deviations. For each deviation it records the causes, the events that follow, the consequences without credit for safeguards, the existing safeguards, and the risk after safeguards (S × L). Rows above the tolerable level go to LOPA in the same worksheet: initiating-event frequency, enabling conditions and conditional modifiers, independent protection layers with their PFD, and the mitigated frequency compared with the tolerable event likelihood for the severity. Open points go to the Parking Lot; actions become recommendations with an owner and a due date.

N1.causes:
SDV-101 closes (SIS trip or instrument-air failure)
wells shut in upstream
choke HV-100 closed in error
N1.cons: Production lost. V-101 pressure falls slowly: 10.0 → 6.6 bar g in 30 min with the choke shut (model run); levels drop; no hazard

N1.causes:
Choke HV-100 opened wide (HIC-100 error, trim eroded)
another well brought on line (+20 %)
gas breakthrough (gas rate up to +60 %)
N1.cons: More gas than PV-110 passes: with the choke at 100 % the model reached 10.99 bar g and flared 3.7 kSm³/h. If both gas outlets are also blocked, V-101 goes above its 12.0 bar g design: rupture, jet fire
N1.notes:
Worked example
LOPA (worked example): values from the OTS LOPA tab, scenario LP-1, and teaching defaults. Not credited: PIC-111 / PV-111 (the cause is a BPCS failure; one BPCS credit per scenario) and the PI-111 HI alarm (seconds to the trip, too fast for an operator). PSV-119 (PFD 0.01) may be credited only after R01 confirms the relief case: then f_mit = 3.08e-07 per year, which meets the TEL.

ie.d: HIC-100 / choke HV-100 driven wide open: BPCS loop failure (generic CCPS value, as the LOPA tab, LP-1)

en.d: Both gas outlets blocked at the same time: export route lost and PV-111 not opening (assumed for teaching)

cm.d: Probability of ignition (LOPA tab LP-1, assumed generic)
Probability that someone is in the area (LOPA tab LP-1, assumed)

N1.causes:
Wells shut in against a closed SDV-101 (pressure settles to the shut-in pressure, assumed above 30 bar g)
wrong manifold line-up
N1.cons: SDV-101 and HV-100 see the full shut-in pressure; if the specification break is wrong, a rupture upstream of the choke
Less flow and production; no hazard

N1.causes:
Cold flowline (rain, low rate): TI-101 falls 35 → 22 °C
Joule–Thomson cooling across the choke
N1.cons: More heat needed in E-101; colder separation and off-spec oil if steam is limited; hydrates could block the choke (not modelled)

N1.causes: Sand production from a well (up to 1.5 m³/h)
N1.cons: Erosion of the choke and elbows: loss of containment and jet fire; sand fills the V-101 inlet section and blocks the water nozzle

N1.causes: A well waters out: water cut 33 → 50 %
N1.cons: Interface rises; more water through LV-120; more oil in the water

N1.dev: Back-flow from V-101 to the manifold
N1.causes: Manifold pressure falls below V-101 pressure with SDV-101 open
N1.cons: Gas from V-101 back into the flowline; small, no hazard at 30 bar g normal manifold pressure

N1.dev: Liquid slugs with the well stream
N1.causes:
Pigging
terrain slugging on a long flowline at low rate
N1.cons: Inlet level rises (a full slug reached 1236 mm in the model, no trip); carry-over to K-201; inlet trip if the level reaches 1500 mm
